session.question: In the study, how did PC affect EE, and what was the impact of EE and SI on SS?
session.answer:
Perceived curiosity (PC) had a significant positive effect on effort expectancy (EE), meaning that higher curiosity was associated with changes in how easy or effortful students perceived the Metaverse technology to be. (alkhwaldi2024investigatingthesocial chunk 1)

In contrast, both effort expectancy (EE) and social influence (SI) had no significant impact on social sustainability (SS). Thus, neither EE nor SI directly predicted students’ perceptions of the Metaverse’s social sustainability in Jordanian higher education institutions. (alkhwaldi2024investigatingthesocial chunk 1)

In contrast, both effort expectancy (EE) and social influence (SI) had no significant impact on social sustainability (SS). session.context:
pqac-0c461480: The study integrated UTAUT factors with perceived curiosity (PC) and extraversion (EXT) to examine students’ perceptions of Metaverse social sustainability in Jordanian higher education institutions. Survey data from 422 students were analyzed using SEM. The results showed that PC significantly affected effort expectancy (EE), indicating that higher curiosity was associated with changes in how easy or effortful the technology was perceived to be. However, both EE and social influence (SI) were found to have no significant impact on social sustainability (SS) of the Metaverse in this context.
From Abeer F. Alkhwaldi. Investigating the social sustainability of immersive virtual technologies in higher educational institutions: students’ perceptions toward metaverse technology. Sustainability, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su16020934, doi:10.3390/su16020934.

pqac-c544e5d0: The study integrated perceived curiosity (PC), effort expectancy (EE), social influence (SI), and social sustainability (SS) in a UTAUT-based model. Results from SEM showed that PC significantly affected EE. However, EE and SI were reported to have no significant impact on SS. In other words, curiosity helped shape effort expectancy, but neither effort expectancy nor social influence directly predicted students’ perceptions toward the social sustainability of Metaverse technology in higher education.
From Abeer F. Alkhwaldi. Investigating the social sustainability of immersive virtual technologies in higher educational institutions: students’ perceptions toward metaverse technology. Sustainability, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su16020934, doi:10.3390/su16020934.

pqac-f04a36a4: The paper examines how digital transformation indicators affect sustainability performance using structural equation modeling. It reports that the company’s digital transformation indicators positively influence economic and social performance and improve environmental protection by decreasing pollution. The study also builds a hierarchy of digitization indicators based on their impact on sustainability indicators. However, in the excerpt provided, the specific abbreviations PC, EE, SI, and SS are not defined, and the exact directional effects between them are not stated. The available text only supports a general positive influence of digital transformation on sustainability-related outcomes.
From Anca Mehedinţu and Georgeta Șoavă. Approach to the impact of digital technologies on sustainability reporting through structural equation modeling and artificial neural networks. Electronics, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics12092048, doi:10.3390/electronics12092048.
